---
title: "Why the exact computation is cheap"
subtitle: "Catalog C-10, C-12, C-11"
description: "Three facts that let every number on this site be computed live: K_J given alpha is a sum of Bernoulli draws, the Gamma mixture is a finite sum over a grid, and so a calibration is a Newton solve in milliseconds."
toc: false
---

Every number on this site is computed in your browser, exactly, while you move a slider.
Three facts make that possible.

## 1. Given alpha, the number of clusters is a sum of coin flips

In the Chinese restaurant process, unit i opens a new table with probability
p_i = alpha / (alpha + i − 1), independently of the other units. So K_J = B_1 + … + B_J with
B_i ~ Bernoulli(p_i). Its mean and variance are sums, and its pmf is a convolution that takes
J² steps. At alpha = 1 and J = 500 the convolution lands on the Antoniak pmf from Stirling
numbers to within 1e-10, and E K_500 = H_500 = 6.79.

```{=html}
<div id="w-bsum" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/bernoulli-sum.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxBsum = DPX["bernoulli-sum"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-bsum"), { J: 500, alpha: 1 });
</script>
```

## 2. Over alpha, the prior is a finite mixture

A Gamma prior on alpha mixes these pmfs. On a quadrature grid of alpha nodes the mixture is a
weighted sum, and a few hundred nodes are enough: below, the J = 50 TSMM prior
Gamma(1.4082, 1.0770) starts at 20 nodes; drag the node count up and watch the error vanish.

```{=html}
<div id="w-mix" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/bundles/gamma-mixing.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxMixFast = DPX["gamma-mixing"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-mix"), { a: 1.4082, b: 1.077, J: 50, n: 20 });
</script>
```

## 3. So a calibration takes milliseconds

TSMM needs the mean and variance of K_J and their derivatives, each one pass over that grid, and
Newton needs about six passes. The badges below time it in this browser.

```{=html}
<div id="w-time" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/bundles/timing-badges.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxTime = DPX["timing-badges"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-time"), {});
</script>
```

Because a calibration costs milliseconds, J and mu_K can be swept freely: the "Sweep" button
calibrates 150 targets at once. MCMC is still needed to fit the model to data (the paper's
simulation admitted 57,151 fits, each started with four chains of 12,000 iterations), but not
to choose the prior.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The gamma-mixing widget is the same file as on [the Gamma mixing page](../bridge/gamma-mixing.qmd)
(catalog C-12), mounted here with a different starting prior. Times vary by device; they are
medians of five runs after a warm-up.
:::

Standalone versions: [embed/bernoulli-sum.html](../../embed/bernoulli-sum.html) (for example
`?J=500&alpha=1`) and [embed/timing-badges.html](../../embed/timing-badges.html).
